Subject: Notice of subcontractor addition + order form pass-through language

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

Quick heads-up: DataFlux will be engaging CloudOps Ltd. as a limited subprocessor to handle encrypted log storage and ephemeral compute for part of our analytics pipeline. This change affects the order form pass-through language we ship to customers (we plan to surface CloudOps in a subprocessor list and add a short pass-through clause to the Order Form).

High level:
- Subprocessor: CloudOps Ltd. (no access to customer application data; only encrypted logs and ephemeral batch transformations)
- Proposed pass-through: brief clause to allow DataFlux to engage CloudOps for storage/processing under DataFlux's DPA obligations
- Timeline: deployment expected 2028-04-01; we can hold off on referencing CloudOps in any new OFs until we have contract language agreed

Attaching a short notice doc and the SOC2 snapshot for CloudOps.

Attachments: dataflux_subproc_notice.pdf (PDF), soc2_snapshot_2027.pdf (PDF)

Can your team review for any redline blockers (particularly around audit rights, notification timing, and order form flow-down obligations)? Samir is on copy for procurement questions.

Thanks,
Elena

Thanks Soojin — attaching the proposed Order Form addendum with our tracked changes. Key clarifications up front:
- CloudOps will only store encrypted logs and will not have keys to decrypt customer payloads.
- CloudOps will not provide downstream ML features or customer-facing inference; it's strictly storage/ephemeral compute for batch analytics.
- We are proposing a 30-day notice for planned additions; immediate notice for any security incidents impacting Redwood workloads.

Attachments: proposed_orderform_addendum_redlines.docx (Word), soc2_snapshot_2027.pdf (PDF)
DocuSign stub: https://docusign.example.com/DFX/OF-addendum/placeholder (will publish once legal agrees)

Please confirm whether the attached language (particularly section 2.3 pass-through and section 5.1 audit language) is acceptable or needs redline. We can narrow text on audit rights and carveouts if you prefer a DPA annex route instead of embedding in the OF.

Regards,
Elena
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@dataflux.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-10T16:22:00Z
Subject: RE: Notice of subcontractor addition + order form pass-through language

Elena / Soojin — Legal has reviewed the draft addendum. High level comments (we kept these intentionally high-level to accelerate alignment):

1) Audit & evidence: The current OF addendum references "reasonable audit rights." For Redwood customers we need either: (a) contractual audit rights on CloudOps limited to logs relevant to Redwood services and under Redwood supervision; or (b) express obligation for DataFlux to provide audit artifacts (log extracts, attestation) within 15 business days on request. Which can you accept?

2) Notification window: 30 days for planned additions is acceptable. For security incidents impacting Redwood we require immediate notification (within 24 hours) + weekly updates until resolution.

3) Flow-down language / indemnity: The addendum should include explicit flow-down of DataFlux's security obligations (encryption at rest/in transit, key custody, access controls) and a limited indemnity for breaches caused by CloudOps' gross negligence or willful misconduct. DataFlux should also confirm CloudOps' access controls and least-privilege policies.

4) Subprocessor list updates: Please commit to a public subprocessor registry URL and an internal change log that lists effective dates; this avoids OF churn when minor housekeeping occurs.

5) Scope limitation: If CloudOps will never process customer-provided content beyond encrypted logs, add a narrow scope clause to prevent mission creep.

Procurement ask for Connor: Please confirm whether DataFlux's addendum changes the pricing or requires an order form amendment on commercial terms.

Please send formal redlines back to legal@redwood.com (we prefer a tracked Word doc) and send DocuSign to legal@redwood.com once text is agreed. If DataFlux prefers, we can accept a DPA annex that references CloudOps instead of embedding long OF language — whichever speeds execution while preserving audit rights.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts
